items.denn: denn keeps the verb in second place. Here bin is last: weil.
items.deshalb: deshalb is an adverb that gives a result and does not send the verb to the end.

items.hat er recht: After dass the conjugated verb goes to the end.
items.er hat recht: The verb must be last: dass er recht hat.

items.dass: dass reports a statement. A yes/no question becomes a Nebensatz with ob.
items.wann: wann asks for a time. The question here is yes/no.

items.Wenn: wenn is for repeated events, the present and the future. One past event is als.
items.Wann: wann is a question word, not a conjunction.

items.Als: als is only for one event in the past.
items.Weil: weil gives a reason. Here Zeit haben is the condition: wenn.

items.wir bleiben: A Nebensatz at the start fills the first position, so the verb comes next: bleiben wir.
items.wir bleiben nicht: The verb must follow the comma directly. nicht would also change the meaning.

items.um: um … zu needs the same subject and an Infinitiv. Here there is a full clause: ich … kann.
items.dass: dass reports a statement. It does not give a purpose.

items.damit: damit gives a purpose. so … dass gives a result.
items.weil: weil gives a reason. so laut … dass shows the result.

items.Weil: weil gives a reason. Rain is not a reason to go for a walk.
items.Damit: damit gives a purpose, not a contrast.

items.obwohl: obwohl marks a contrast. Bad sleep is the reason for being tired.
items.damit: damit gives a purpose, not a reason.

items.habe: habe is the present. Before the Präteritum ging, use the Plusquamperfekt: hatte gegessen.
items.war: essen forms its Perfekt with haben, so hatte, not war.

items.damit: damit gives a purpose, not a time.
items.obwohl: obwohl means „although“. The sentence is about time: sobald.

items.ist gekommen: In a Nebensatz the conjugated verb goes last: gekommen ist.
items.gekommen hat: kommen forms its Perfekt with sein, not haben.

items.kann kommen: In a Nebensatz the conjugated verb goes last: kommen kann.
items.kann kommen können: Only one infinitive plus the modal verb: kommen kann.

items.hat: hat goes with er, sie, es. With du it is hast.

items.wohnt: wohnt goes with er, sie, es. With ich it is wohne.
items.wohnen: wohnen goes with wir and sie (plural).

items.wird gebaut: In a Nebensatz the conjugated verb goes last: gebaut wird.
items.gebaut werden: werden is the plural form. The verb must agree with das Haus: wird.

items.damit: damit gives a purpose. indem says how: by cooking himself.
items.obwohl: obwohl marks a contrast. Cooking himself is the way he saves.

items.damit: damit gives a purpose. The sentence says she left without him being able to speak.
items.indem: indem says how something happens, by doing something.

items.dass: dass reports a statement. The question was yes/no: ob.
items.wenn: wenn is a condition. Here we ask whether.

items.arbeiten müssen hat: In a Nebensatz hat comes before the double infinitive.
items.hat müssen arbeiten: The infinitives keep their order: arbeiten müssen.

items.machen können hätte: With a double infinitive, hätte comes before it.
items.hätte können machen: The infinitives keep their order: machen können.

items.habe: habe is present or Konjunktiv I. An unreal past condition needs the Konjunktiv II: hätte.
items.würde: würde goes with an infinitive. It cannot combine with the participle gewusst.

items.hatte: ankommen forms its Perfekt with sein: war angekommen.
items.wurde: wurde is the Passiv auxiliary. This sentence is not passive.
